questions.question_text: Cytoarchitectural abnormalities have been reported in the entorhinal cortex in schizophrenia. The changes that are suggestive of disturbed development include all of the following, with the exception of

options.text: Paucity of neurons in superficial layers
Increased density of neurons in the deeper layer

correct_answer.text: Increased density of neurons in the deeper layer

correct_answers.text: Increased density of neurons in the deeper layer

questions.explanation: Arnold et al. (1991) have proposed that all of the aforementioned are responsible for the disturbed development that has led to the onset of schizophrenia with the exception of option (e). It has also been proposed that schizophrenic post-mortem brains had a smaller neuron size in the hippocampal regions of the subiculum, CA1 and layer II of the entorhinal cortex.

questions.question_text: A neurologist has been called to the emergency service to assess a 70-year-old man. It was noted that the man was unable to speak and comprehend speech. Which terminology best describes this?
questions.explanation: Dysphasia, paraphasia or aphasia refers to disturbances in the comprehension and expression of speech as a result of underlying brain lesions. Broca’s area coordinates the organs of speech to produce coherent sounds, while Wernicke’s area is involved in making sense of speech and language.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old male has been started on a new medication known as quetiapine to help him with his symptoms. He has been measuring his blood pressure daily and he has noted that his blood pressure is now lower when he takes the medication. This is due to the effect of

options.text: Blockage of the alpha-1 adrenergic receptors
Blockage of the alpha-2 adrenergic receptors

correct_answer.text: Blockage of the alpha-1 adrenergic receptors

correct_answers.text: Blockage of the alpha-1 adrenergic receptors

questions.explanation: It has been shown that some tricyclic antidepressants and antipsychotics, including quetiapine, cause sedation and postural hypotension as a result of blockage of the alpha-1 adrenergic receptors.

questions.question_text: A couple is considering adopting a child after multiple failures with artificial fertilization. They found a 2-year-old boy whom they were keen to adopt. However, they realized that the child’s biological parents were alcoholic. What is the risk ratio of the child having similar alcohol dependence?
questions.explanation: Adoption studies have found that there is at least a four-fold increase in the risk of the child developing alcohol dependence if the biological parents are alcoholic.

questions.question_text: Based on epidemiological studies, roughly what percentage of patients with late paraphrenia would resemble that with paranoid schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: It has been estimated that around 60% of patients with late paraphrenia actually resemble those with paranoid schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: The ICD-10 and the DSM-5 both have a specific constellation of symptoms for the diagnosis of borderline personality disorder. Which of the following clinical signs and symptoms would improve over time?
questions.explanation: With regards to the course and prognosis of borderline personality disorder, it has been noted that impulsiveness tends to improve significantly over time. Affective instability is associated with the least amount of improvement.

questions.question_text: A 6-year-old child was lost whilst he was out shopping with his mother. Initially, he showed marked signs of distress when he realized that he was lost, but when his mother returned, he began to ignore her. Based on Ainsworth’s theory, what particular type of attachment would this be?
questions.explanation: Children with avoidant attachment keep their distance from the mother and may ignore her on reunion. Clinically, avoidant attachment can lead to poor social functioning and may be associated with aggressive behaviour later in life.

questions.question_text: Based on epidemiological studies, roughly what percentage of people with schizophrenia would have an onset older than 60 years?
questions.explanation: It has been estimated that roughly 1.5% of people with schizophrenia have an onset older than 60 years.

questions.question_text: Antidepressants that act on which one of the following receptors might cause weight gain?
questions.explanation: Blockade of histamine H1 receptors is associated with weight gain and sedation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about serotonin is incorrect?

options.text: Serotonin is synthesized from dietary amino acid l-tryptophan.

Depletion of serotonin could be achieved by inhibiting tryptophan hydroxylase, removing l-tryptophan from the diet or adding natural amino acids such as alanine to compete for the transport process with l-tryptophan.
The release of 5-HT is dependent on calcium ions.
When depressed patients take SSRI, it would not lead to a reduction in 5-HT levels in the platelets.
Serotonin is taken back into the neurons and degraded by monoamine oxidase (MAO)-A.

correct_answer.text: When depressed patients take SSRI, it would not lead to a reduction in 5-HT levels in the platelets.

correct_answers.text: When depressed patients take SSRI, it would not lead to a reduction in 5-HT levels in the platelets.

questions.explanation: Most peripheral serotonin is stored in platelets. When patients take SSRIs, platelet serotonin levels fall while plasma serotonin levels increase.

questions.question_text: The consultant psychiatrist has decided to start one of his patients on a MAO-I antidepressant in order to help him with his mood symptoms. He cautions the patient to be wary of his dietary intake. Which of the following should the patient avoid?
questions.explanation: Foods high in tyramine, such as cheese, must be avoided when taking MAO-I antidepressants to prevent hypertensive crisis.

questions.question_text: All of the following disorders are caused by trisomy, with the exception of
questions.explanation: Cri-du-chat syndrome results from a partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5, not trisomy.

questions.question_text: Epidemiological studies have shown which of the following findings to be incorrect for bipolar disorder?

options.text: Bipolar disorder is equally common in both males and females.
Rapid cycling disorder is more common in males.
The age of onset of bipolar disorder is much earlier as compared to unipolar depression.
There is a significant comorbidity with substance misuse and this has been estimated to be as high as 50%.
On average, around 25%–50% of bipolar patients commit suicide.

correct_answer.text: Rapid cycling disorder is more common in males.

correct_answers.text: Rapid cycling disorder is more common in males.

questions.explanation: Rapid cycling bipolar disorder is actually more common in females, not males.

questions.question_text: Which of the following theories explains how a child learns about what is considered to be gender appropriate for his or her anatomical sex?
questions.explanation: Social learning theory posits that children learn gender roles through observation, imitation and reinforcement.

questions.question_text: Long-acting benzodiazepines would include all of the following, with the exception of
questions.explanation: Temazepam (and lorazepam) are intermediate-acting benzodiazepines; the others listed are long-acting.

questions.question_text: A consultant psychiatrist decides to start a patient on a combination of clozapine and carbamazepine. The pharmacist reviewed the prescription and decides to call upon the consultant as she is worried about the patient developing which one of the following?

options.text: Reduced total white blood cell count

correct_answer.text: Reduced total white blood cell count

correct_answers.text: Reduced total white blood cell count

questions.explanation: Both clozapine and carbamazepine can suppress bone marrow, increasing the risk of agranulocytosis and a reduction in total white blood cell count.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a known mechanism of placebo effect?
questions.explanation: Placebo effects involve multiple mechanisms, including homeostatic regulation, classical conditioning, operant conditioning, and cognitive-affective behavioural processes.

questions.question_text: Children with autism are believed to have impaired developments of their theory of mind. At roughly what age would children develop a theory of the mind?
questions.explanation: Theory of mind typically develops around the age of 4 years, when children can understand that others have beliefs and intentions different from their own.

questions.question_text: In borderline personality disorder, it is known that impulsivity improves significantly over time. Poorer prognosis has been associated with all of the following, with the exception of
questions.explanation: Chronic depression is not associated with a poorer prognosis; in fact, individuals with chronic depressive features may respond better to treatment if motivated and in a stable environment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the biosynthesis and metabolism of GABA is incorrect?

options.text: GABA is derived from glutamic acid via the action of glutamic acid decarboxylase.
It would require pyridoxal phosphate that is a vitamin B6 co-factor.
In schizophrenia, there is an increased expression of the messenger RNA for the enzyme in the prefrontal cortex.
The metabolic breakdown of GABA to glutamic acid involves the action of GABA transaminase.
GABA transaminase is often the target for anticonvulsants and inhibition of this enzyme would lead to an increase in GABA levels and prevent convulsions.

correct_answer.text: In schizophrenia, there is an increased expression of the messenger RNA for the enzyme in the prefrontal cortex.

correct_answers.text: In schizophrenia, there is an increased expression of the messenger RNA for the enzyme in the prefrontal cortex.

questions.explanation: In schizophrenia, there is a decreased—not increased—expression of the glutamic acid decarboxylase mRNA in the prefrontal cortex.

questions.question_text: Clomipramine, imipramine and trimipramine belong to which specific class of tricyclic antidepressant?
questions.explanation: Clomipramine, imipramine and trimipramine are all part of the iminodibenzyl class of tricyclic antidepressants.

questions.question_text: Fragile X syndrome is due to

options.text: Failure of FMR1 gene transcription due to hypermethylation
Failure of t-RNA to bind to the correct amino acids

correct_answer.text: Failure of FMR1 gene transcription due to hypermethylation

correct_answers.text: Failure of FMR1 gene transcription due to hypermethylation

questions.explanation: Fragile X syndrome results from hypermethylation of the FMR1 gene promoter, leading to failure of FMR1 transcription and absence of its protein product.

questions.question_text: What is the estimated increase in risk of a child developing alcoholism if his father is dependent on alcohol?
questions.explanation: If the father is alcohol-dependent, the child’s risk of developing alcoholism is estimated at about 80%, roughly a fourfold increase over baseline.

questions.question_text: In this form of therapy, the therapy focuses on four core areas, including role transitions, interpersonal difficulties, interpersonal deficits and grief. Which one of the following best describes the therapy?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal therapy (IPT) focuses on grief, interpersonal disputes, role transitions and interpersonal deficits as core areas of intervention.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a rate-limiting enzyme in the synthesis of dopamine?
questions.explanation: Tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting enzyme in dopamine synthesis, converting tyrosine to L-DOPA.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the rate of absorption is incorrect?

options.text: The rate of absorption is dependent on the particular form of the drug.
The rate of absorption is dependent on the pKa of the drug.
The rate of absorption is dependent on the particle size of the drug.
The rate of absorption is independent of the ambient pH.
The rate of absorption is dependent on the rate of blood flow through the tissue.

correct_answer.text: The rate of absorption is independent of the ambient pH.

correct_answers.text: The rate of absorption is independent of the ambient pH.

questions.explanation: The rate of absorption is influenced by ambient pH, because drug solubility and ionization vary with pH.

questions.question_text: It has been shown that mania in patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) indicates poor prognosis and would affect the adherence to antiretroviral drugs. Which one of the following statements about the application of mood stabilizers in HIV-infected patients is incorrect?

options.text: When lithium is used, it is necessary to monitor closely for neurotoxicity and gastrointestinal side effects.
Sodium valproate is effective in treating mania in patients infected with HIV.
The usage of carbamazepine would result in an elevated risk of pancytopenia in HIV-infected patients.
It is important to note that carbamazepine would induce its own metabolism and this would decrease not only its own levels, but that of other drugs as well.

questions.explanation: Lithium carbonate is often poorly tolerated in HIV-infected patients, especially those with renal impairment; close monitoring for neurotoxicity and gastrointestinal side effects is essential.

questions.question_text: The cognitive component of cognitive behavioural therapy usually involves all of the following, with the exception of

options.text: Finding evidence for the cognitions identified

questions.explanation: Social skills training is part of the behavioural component of CBT, not the cognitive component.

questions.question_text: Which of the following personality disorders is known to be the most common amongst inpatients?
questions.explanation: Borderline personality disorder is the most common personality disorder among psychiatric inpatients, with a prevalence of around 20%.

questions.question_text: A patient presents to the emergency services with the following symptoms: unilateral pupil that is moderately dilated, with poor reaction to light and slow reaction to accommodation. Which of the following is the correct clinical diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Holmes–Adie pupil typically presents with a moderately dilated pupil, poor light reaction and slow near-response; deep tendon reflexes (e.g., knee jerk) are often diminished or absent.

questions.question_text: A core trainee has been asked to assess a patient who was opioid dependent in the emergency department. He is unsure what drugs are commonly used for the treatment of opioid dependence. Based on your understanding, which of the following is incorrect due to its potential side effects?
questions.explanation: Levo-alpha-acetylmethadol (LAAM) carries a risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes, making its use problematic despite its long duration of action.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Huntington’s disease is incorrect?

options.text: It is an autosomal recessive disease
It is a progressive, inherited neurodegenerative disease
The clinical features include abnormal involuntary movements and cognitive deterioration
There might be further progression to death and dementia over a course of 10–20 years
The gene responsible is located on the short arm of chromosome 4

correct_answer.text: It is an autosomal recessive disease

correct_answers.text: It is an autosomal recessive disease

questions.explanation: Huntington’s disease is an autosomal dominant disorder, not recessive.

questions.question_text: Which of the following personality disorders is considered to be relatively uncommon in outpatients?
questions.explanation: Schizoid personality disorder is relatively rare among psychiatric outpatients compared to other personality disorders.

questions.question_text: A psychotherapist mentions to his client, ‘If I were in your position, I might have a hard time dealing with those difficult people in your company’. Which particular type of interviewing technique is he using?
questions.explanation: Affirmation is the technique of validating the client’s feelings or experiences, confirming that their reaction is understandable.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Introns are not expressed in the final protein product
Telomeres play a key role in chromosome assortment during cell division
The lagging strand is formed continuously, moving in the 5ʹ to 3ʹ direction during DNA replication
The leading strand is formed in blocks during DNA replication

correct_answer.text: Introns are not expressed in the final protein product

correct_answers.text: Introns are not expressed in the final protein product

questions.explanation: Introns are non-coding sequences that are transcribed but removed during RNA splicing and do not appear in the final protein product.

questions.question_text: A core trainee wants to consider referring one of the patients he has seen and diagnosed with depressive disorder for brief psychodynamic psychotherapy. He wonders which one of the following psychiatric conditions would not benefit from brief dynamic psychotherapy intervention?
questions.explanation: Severe dependence on substances is a contraindication for brief dynamic psychotherapy, as it compromises the patient’s capacity to engage in insight-oriented work.

questions.question_text: Adoption studies for depressive disorder have shown that there is an increase in the rate for affective disorder among the relatives of index adoptees by roughly what percentage?
questions.explanation: Adoption studies indicate approximately an eight-fold increase in affective disorder among relatives of adoptees with depression.

questions.question_text: There is an association between schizophrenia and the following genes, with the exception of which one of the following?
questions.explanation: While several genes have been implicated in schizophrenia, the dopamine D2 receptor gene has not shown a consistent association.

questions.question_text: This is a clinical condition involving a pupil due to rapidly increasing unilateral intracranial pressure. Which of the following is the correct clinical diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Hutchinson’s pupil (fixed, dilated pupil on one side) occurs when rapidly rising intracranial pressure compresses the oculomotor nerve (III), causing an unreactive dilated pupil.

questions.question_text: A drug addict was involved in a gang fight and sustained an open laceration of his elbow. He believes that one of the drugs which he has been abusing might help to relieve his pain. Which one of the following drugs does have pain-relieving properties?
questions.explanation: Cocaine blocks dopamine reuptake, leading to analgesic and local anesthetic effects; it can relieve pain by blocking sodium channels in nerves.

questions.question_text: The female-to-male ratio for post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) has been estimated to be
questions.explanation: Epidemiological data estimate a female-to-male ratio of approximately 2:1 for PTSD.

questions.question_text: Body dysmorphic disorder tends to affect females more than males. The comorbid psychiatric disorder includes all of the following, with the exception of
questions.explanation: Depression, trichotillomania, social phobia and OCD are common comorbidities of body dysmorphic disorder; eating disorders are not typically associated.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not one of the factors that would render a client suitable for brief dynamic psychotherapy?

options.text: Client has strong motivation to understand more about the influence of the past on the present
Client has sufficient ego strength to deal with the topics that are discussed
Client has the ability to tolerate frustration
Client does not have the capacity to sustain previous relationships

correct_answer.text: Client does not have the capacity to sustain previous relationships

correct_answers.text: Client does not have the capacity to sustain previous relationships

questions.explanation: A key selection criterion is that the client must have the capacity to form and sustain relationships; lack of this capacity contraindicates brief dynamic psychotherapy.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old black African man suffers from hypertension and bipolar disorder. His GP wants to consult you about the safest diuretic to prescribe, as he takes lithium. Your recommendation is
questions.explanation: Potassium-sparing diuretics such as amiloride are preferred with lithium, as thiazides may unpredictably raise lithium levels and loop diuretics are less effective for hypertension.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old woman with agoraphobia is gradually exposed to crowded areas while relaxed. The periods of exposure gradually become longer and longer until she can confidently go to the market without an anxious response. This phenomenon is known as
questions.explanation: Systematic desensitization involves graded exposure to the feared stimulus while maintaining relaxation, progressively increasing the duration or intensity of exposure.

questions.question_text: The big five factors of personality do not include which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Big Five are openness to experience, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism; carelessness is not a factor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a relative contraindication for brief dynamic psychotherapy?
questions.explanation: Partial insight alone is not a contraindication. True contraindications include psychotic disorders, severe self-harm risk and severe substance dependence.

questions.question_text: It has been shown that inheritance plays a significant role in the transmission of bipolar disorder. What is the estimated heritability of bipolar disorder?
questions.explanation: Heritability of bipolar disorder is estimated at around 80%–90%, indicating a strong genetic contribution.

questions.question_text: For patients who have been diagnosed with normal-pressure hydrocephalus, which of their symptoms would improve after shunting?
questions.explanation: Gait disturbances are the most responsive symptom in normal-pressure hydrocephalus after ventriculoperitoneal shunting.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not one of the factors that could help to optimize a patient’s compliance?

options.text: Educating the patient about his or her medications
Reducing the number of tablets to be taken
Considering using parenteral or depot administration
Allowing the patient and not the family members to take ownership

correct_answer.text: Allowing the patient and not the family members to take ownership

correct_answers.text: Allowing the patient and not the family members to take ownership

questions.explanation: Involving family members in treatment planning and encouraging shared ownership can improve medication compliance; excluding them does not help.

questions.question_text: The clinical features of fragile X syndrome are due to the failure of FMR1 gene transcription due to hypermethylation, thus resulting in the absence of the FMR1 gene protein. In addition, associated changes have been found such as the presence of a sequence of repeats. Which of the following sequence is being repeated?
questions.explanation: Fragile X syndrome is associated with a trinucleotide repeat expansion of the sequence CGG in the FMR1 gene.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not one of the risk factors for depression that has been proposed previously by Brown and Harris in their study?

options.text: Having three or more children under the age of 11 years old

questions.explanation: Brown and Harris identified unemployment, recent separation, lack of a confiding relationship and multiple young children as key risk factors, but bereavement was not one of their proposed factors.

questions.question_text: During a session of brief dynamic psychotherapy, the client is silent when asked to speak about his previous experiences. Which one of the following negative reactions is this considered to be?
questions.explanation: Silence or refusal to discuss material can be a form of resistance, reflecting ambivalence about exploring difficult topics.

questions.question_text: Based on the experiments conducted by H. Wimmer and J. Perner, the theory of mind develops after the age of
questions.explanation: Children typically reliably pass false-belief tests demonstrating theory of mind by around 4 years of age.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the Hayling and Brixton Test is false?

options.text: People with frontal lobe impairment perform poorly on the Hayling and Brixton Test.
The Hayling and Brixton Test was developed by Paul Burgess and Tim Shallice.
The Brixton Test is a spatial awareness test.
The Brixton Test is a response initiation and response suppression test.
The Hayling Test is a sentence completion test.

correct_answer.text: The Brixton Test is a response initiation and response suppression test.

correct_answers.text: The Brixton Test is a response initiation and response suppression test.

questions.explanation: The Brixton Test assesses rule acquisition and shifting (a spatial anticipation task), whereas the Hayling Test assesses response initiation and suppression via sentence completion.

questions.question_text: A 14-year-old female adolescent develops non-epileptic fits when she is stressed. Her response was initially reinforced by attention from her teachers and peers. The non-epileptic fit is subsequently ignored until the non-epileptic fits no longer occur. This phenomenon is known as
questions.explanation: When a learned behaviour stops occurring because reinforcement is withdrawn, the behaviour is said to undergo extinction.

questions.question_text: During a session of brief dynamic psychotherapy, the client decided to explore more about the therapist’s personal and private information. Which of the following negative reactions is this considered to be?
questions.explanation: Acting in involves the client directing attention toward the therapist, such as seeking personal information or approval.

questions.question_text: The neuroanatomical area involved in face recognition is
questions.explanation: The fusiform gyrus, particularly the fusiform face area, is specialized for processing facial identity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the Camberwell Family Interview is false?

options.text: Both verbal responses and nonverbal cues are used to assess expressed emotion.
It has five components: critical comments, hostility, emotional overinvolvement, warmth and positive comments.
It is used to assess expressed emotion.
The Camberwell Family Interview does not measure the perception of the patient.

correct_answer.text: The Camberwell Family Interview does not measure the perception of the patient.

correct_answers.text: The Camberwell Family Interview does not measure the perception of the patient.

questions.explanation: The CFI does include assessment of the patient’s perceived experience of family attitudes; it is not limited solely to the relatives’ expressed emotion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not part of Beck’s cognitive model of depression?
questions.explanation: Beck’s model emphasizes core beliefs, underlying assumptions, cognitive distortions, the cognitive triad and automatic thoughts; attachment issues are not a central component.

questions.question_text: Specific reading disorder has been defined as a child having a score on reading or comprehension that is at least two standard deviations below that expected for the child’s chronological age and intelligence. What is the estimated prevalence of this condition amongst the 9–11-year-olds in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: The prevalence of specific reading disorder in UK children aged 9–11 years is around 4%.

questions.question_text: A core trainee was asked to review an intravenous drug abuser. He noted that the patient seemed to have marked impairments in his memory, especially with regards to word finding difficulties. Which one of the following might be the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: HIV-associated dementia often presents with word-finding difficulties, psychomotor slowing and subcortical features in long-term intravenous drug users.

questions.question_text: A 15-year-old boy was brought into the emergency department presenting with raised blood pressure, palpitations, and enlarged pupils. He was agitated and shouting that he saw spirits chasing after him. His friend who accompanied him mentioned that he had been ingesting ‘bath salts’ in the pub. Which of the following mechanisms does ‘bath salts’ act upon that could have accounted for the boy’s presentation?

options.text: Provokes release of dopamine in the mesolimbic system

questions.explanation: The active component in so-called ‘bath salts’ (e.g., MDPV) inhibits reuptake of dopamine and norepinephrine, causing sympathomimetic and psychotic effects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis is incorrect?

options.text: It usually involves two stages of cell divisions.
Chromosomal division takes place once during meiosis, and the resultant gametes are haploid.
Recombination takes place during prophase I.
There is an interphase stage in the second stage of cellular division.
The following stages are present in both meiosis I and meiosis II: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase.

correct_answer.text: There is an interphase stage in the second stage of cellular division.

correct_answers.text: There is an interphase stage in the second stage of cellular division.

questions.explanation: There is no interphase between meiosis I and meiosis II; the cell proceeds directly into the second division.

questions.question_text: What has been believed to be the estimated prevalence of personality disorder in the general practice setting?
questions.explanation: Studies estimate that about 20% of patients in general practice meet criteria for a personality disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the objectives of cognitive behavioural therapy is incorrect?

options.text: It helps to alleviate symptoms such as anxiety and depression by helping clients to identify negative cognitions.
It helps to enable clients to challenge negative cognitions.
It helps them to develop alternative and flexible schema.
It helps them to rehearse new cognitive and behavioural responses to difficult situations.
It helps individuals to identify faulty procedures.

correct_answer.text: It helps individuals to identify faulty procedures.

correct_answers.text: It helps individuals to identify faulty procedures.

questions.explanation: Identifying faulty procedures is more characteristic of cognitive analytic therapy; CBT focuses on identifying and restructuring negative cognitions.

questions.question_text: Tardive dyskinesia is associated with supersensitivity of which of the following receptors?
questions.explanation: Tardive dyskinesia is thought to result from upregulation and supersensitivity of dopamine D2 receptors in the striatum.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man with a dual diagnosis of schizophrenia and alcohol dependence is admitted to hospital. He presents with tender hepatomegaly and jaundice. The level of aspartate transaminase (AST) is 250 IU/L (normal value: 3–35 IU/L), and the level of alanine transaminase (ALT) is 150 IU/L (normal value: 3–35 IU/L). He is disturbed by third-person auditory hallucinations and a delusion of persecution. The medical consultant would like to consult you about which antipsychotic to prescribe. Your recommendation is
questions.explanation: Amisulpride is renally excreted and does not require dose adjustment in hepatic impairment, making it safer in a patient with alcohol-related liver disease.

questions.question_text: A core trainee is asked to list down what he thinks are the typical characteristics of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT). Which one of the following statements is incorrect as it is not one of the core characteristics of CBT?

options.text: This is a therapy that focuses on specific issues.
It focuses entirely on the here and now.
Outcomes can be measured only by physiological measures, standardized instruments and self-report measures.

correct_answer.text: Outcomes can be measured only by physiological measures, standardized instruments and self-report measures.

correct_answers.text: Outcomes can be measured only by physiological measures, standardized instruments and self-report measures.

questions.explanation: CBT outcomes can also be measured by behavioral observation and clinical assessment, not solely by physiological or self-report instruments.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old nurse suffers from depression and she needs to work night shifts. She does not like to take medications on a daily basis. Which of the following antidepressants is the most suitable for her?
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine has a long half-life allowing less frequent dosing (e.g., every other day), which may suit someone who works variable shifts.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding duloxetine is true?

options.text: Duloxetine is safe to be co-administered with a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI).
Duloxetine is beneficial to people with urinary stress incontinence.
There is clear evidence that duloxetine offers efficacy benefits over tricyclic antidepressants in the treatment of depression.

correct_answer.text: Duloxetine is beneficial to people with urinary stress incontinence.

correct_answers.text: Duloxetine is beneficial to people with urinary stress incontinence.

questions.explanation: Duloxetine is approved for urinary stress incontinence and increases urethral sphincter tone via noradrenergic mechanisms.

questions.question_text: What is believed to be the estimated prevalence of personality disorder amongst the psychiatric inpatients?
questions.explanation: Approximately 40% of psychiatric inpatients meet criteria for a personality disorder.

questions.question_text: Based on genetic studies, which of the following genes have been associated with Alzheimer’s disease, with the exception of?

options.text: Disrupted in schizophrenia (DISC) gene on chromosome 4

correct_answer.text: Disrupted in schizophrenia (DISC) gene on chromosome 4

correct_answers.text: Disrupted in schizophrenia (DISC) gene on chromosome 4

questions.explanation: The DISC gene on chromosome 4 has been linked to schizophrenia, not Alzheimer’s disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about cognitive impairment and dementia is incorrect?

options.text: Early cognitive impairments occur in around 10% of patients infected with HIV.
Cognitive symptoms include poor memory, concentration impairment, and mental slowing.
Behavioural symptoms include apathy, reduced spontaneity, and social withdrawal.
Motor symptoms include loss of balance, poor coordination, clumsiness, and leg weakness.
The onset of AIDS-associated dementia is usually insidious and occurs later in the course of the illness when there is significant immunosuppression.

correct_answer.text: Early cognitive impairments occur in around 10% of patients infected with HIV.

correct_answers.text: Early cognitive impairments occur in around 10% of patients infected with HIV.

questions.explanation: Early HIV-related cognitive impairment occurs in about 20% of patients, not 10%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about factors affecting the absorption of drugs from the gastrointestinal tract is incorrect?

options.text: Absorption is dependent on the gastric pH.
Absorption is dependent on the intestinal motility.
The presence of food enhances absorption.
Absorption rate is dependent on the area of absorption.
Absorption rate is dependent on the blood flow.

correct_answer.text: The presence of food enhances absorption.

correct_answers.text: The presence of food enhances absorption.

questions.explanation: The presence of food typically delays gastric emptying and can reduce or delay drug absorption rather than enhance it.

questions.question_text: With regards to the genetics of Down’s syndrome, approximately what percentage are a result of translocation involving chromosomes?
questions.explanation: About 4% of Down’s syndrome cases are due to Robertsonian translocations involving chromosome 21 and another acrocentric chromosome.

questions.question_text: Kleptomania is an impulse control disorder that is characterized by repeated failure to resist the impulse to steal, in which the tension is relieved by stealing. What is the gender ratio for kleptomania (females:males)?
questions.explanation: Kleptomania occurs about four times more frequently in females than in males.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old American woman suffering from depression asks to take reboxetine as her British friend has recommended this medication. Which of the following statements regarding reboxetine is true?

options.text: Based on previous study findings, there is clear evidence that reboxetine offers efficacy benefits over other antidepressants in the treatment of depression.
Reboxetine does not have anticholinergic effects.
Reboxetine exerts more influence on serotonin reuptake than on noradrenaline reuptake.
Reboxetine is metabolized by cytochrome P450 3A4.
Reboxetine is available in the United States.

correct_answer.text: Reboxetine is metabolized by cytochrome P450 3A4.

correct_answers.text: Reboxetine is metabolized by cytochrome P450 3A4.

questions.explanation: Reboxetine is a selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor metabolized primarily by CYP3A4.

questions.question_text: The heritability of bipolar disorder is
questions.explanation: Heritability estimates for bipolar disorder are approximately 85%, indicating a strong genetic contribution.

questions.question_text: All of the following are contraindications for cognitive behavioural therapy, with the exception of
questions.explanation: Impulse control disorders are suitable for CBT; the other listed conditions may limit the client’s ability to engage in CBT.

questions.question_text: What is the estimated prevalence of learning disability (which is defined as having an IQ of less than 70) in the general population in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Learning disability (IQ <70) affects around 3.7%–4% of the UK population.

questions.question_text: Translocation involving certain chromosomes might lead to the development of Down’s syndrome. Exchange of chromosomal substance occurs between chromosome 21 and all of the following chromosomes, with the exception of
questions.explanation: Robertsonian translocations causing Down’s syndrome typically involve chromosome 21 and one of 13, 14, 15 or another 21; chromosome 19 is not involved.

questions.question_text: Huntington’s disease is a result of which one of the following proteins?
questions.explanation: Huntington’s disease is caused by CAG repeat expansions in the huntingtin gene, producing a mutant huntingtin protein.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old male has just taken some cannabis that his friend recommended him to try. For how long would the cannabis that he has taken be present and detectable in the blood after just a single dose?
questions.explanation: Δ9-THC is highly lipophilic and can be detectable in blood for up to 20 hours after a single dose.

questions.question_text: With regards to DNA replication, which one of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Replication usually occurs from the 5ʹ to the 3ʹ direction.
New nucleotides are added to the 3ʹ end.
One strand is formed continuously and is known as the leading strand.
The other strand is known as the lagging strand and is composed of 100–1000 nucleotides.
The process is continuous as both the DNA strands are synthesized.

correct_answer.text: The process is continuous as both the DNA strands are synthesized.

correct_answers.text: The process is continuous as both the DNA strands are synthesized.

questions.explanation: DNA replication is semi-discontinuous: the leading strand is synthesized continuously, but the lagging strand is synthesized in Okazaki fragments.

questions.question_text: In order to fulfil the diagnosis of learning disability, the age of onset must be before the age of
questions.explanation: By definition, the onset of intellectual disability must occur before the age of 18, when formal assessment of intellectual functioning is possible.

questions.question_text: Based on the Isle of Wight study, what has been estimated to be the overall prevalence of child psychiatric disorder in middle childhood?
questions.explanation: The Isle of Wight study found a prevalence of child psychiatric disorder of about 6.8% in middle childhood.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders, based on the Isle of Wight study, is known to be the most common amongst middle childhood children?
questions.explanation: Conduct disorder was the most prevalent category of psychiatric disorder in the Isle of Wight cohort.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old woman suffering from depression is currently 35 weeks pregnant and she needs to take antidepressant treatment. Which of the following antidepressants is the most likely to cause withdrawal in the neonate after birth?
questions.explanation: Paroxetine has a relatively short half-life and a high incidence of neonatal discontinuation syndrome when used late in pregnancy.

questions.question_text: A medical student is interested in mirtazapine and she wants to find out more about its pharmacodynamics. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of mirtazapine?
questions.explanation: Mirtazapine enhances noradrenergic and serotonergic neurotransmission primarily by blocking presynaptic α2-adrenergic autoreceptors and heteroreceptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the epidemiology of delusional disorder is incorrect?

options.text: The estimated lifetime risk is between 0.05% and 1.0%.
The mean age of onset is 35 years for males and 45 years for females.
There is equal sex ratio of sufferers.

questions.explanation: Reported remission rates for delusional disorder are lower than 60%; the 60% figure is not supported by epidemiological studies.

questions.question_text: With regards to DNA transcription, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Transcription is the process in which information from the DNA molecule is transcribed onto a primary RNA transcript.
Transcription starts in the upstream locus control region.
Reverse transcription would commence in the downstream locus control region.
Transcription factors are essential as they have specific structural domains such as zinc fingers that could bind to the locus control region.
Concealed strands of DNA would be unfolded and then prepared for transcription.

correct_answer.text: Reverse transcription would commence in the downstream locus control region.

correct_answers.text: Reverse transcription would commence in the downstream locus control region.

questions.explanation: Reverse transcription is the synthesis of DNA from an RNA template and does not commence at the locus control region during normal transcription.

questions.question_text: Research studies (such as that by Weinberger et al.) have looked into the regional cerebral blood flow at rest and during specific neuropsychological testing of schizophrenic patients. Impaired performance on specific task is due to the reduced blood flow to which area of the brain?
questions.explanation: Hypofrontality—reduced blood flow and metabolism in the prefrontal cortex—is linked to cognitive deficits in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: It has been estimated that the risk of dementia is increased amongst first-degree relatives by approximately what incidence?
questions.explanation: First-degree relatives of dementia patients have an approximately 3% higher risk compared to the general population.

questions.question_text: Which of the following neuroanatomical areas is associated with OCD?
questions.explanation: Imaging studies implicate the orbitofrontal cortex in the pathophysiology of obsessive–compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old woman is admitted to the ward and she suffers from borderline personality disorder. Her parents want to know which of the following symptoms is the easiest to treat with medication or psychotherapy. Your answer is
questions.explanation: Impulsive behaviors and self-harm in borderline personality disorder respond better to targeted psychosocial and pharmacological interventions than pervasive identity disturbance or manipulativeness.

questions.question_text: Newly synthesized polypeptide chains could be further modified. All of the following are common posttranslational modification processes, with the exception of
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis is a general degradative process, not a common regulated post-translational modification like disulfide bond formation, cleavage, hydroxylation or phosphorylation.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about the neurochemistry of panic disorder is incorrect?

options.text: There has been shown to be hypersensitivity of the presynaptic alpha-2 receptors and a resultant increase in the adrenergic activity.
There is increased sensitivity of the serotonin receptors and exaggerated postsynaptic receptor response.
There is a reduction in the GABA receptor sensitivity.
Sodium lactate has been implicated in the induction of panic attack.

correct_answer.text: There is increased sensitivity of the serotonin receptors and exaggerated postsynaptic receptor response.

correct_answers.text: There is increased sensitivity of the serotonin receptors and exaggerated postsynaptic receptor response.

questions.explanation: Panic disorder is associated with reduced, not increased, postsynaptic serotonin receptor sensitivity; other statements correctly describe biochemical findings in panic.

questions.question_text: What is the estimated prevalence of depressive symptoms amongst the elderly population in the UK?
questions.explanation: Depressive symptoms in the elderly are common, with a prevalence around 15% in community studies.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old male was involved in a fight in the pub and suffered head injuries. He was taken to the hospital and was treated. He was noted to have disinhibited and antisocial behaviour after the incident. He is likely to have had suffered a head injury involving which part of his cerebral cortex?
questions.explanation: Damage to the right frontal lobe is associated with disinhibition and socially inappropriate or antisocial behaviour.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the MacArthur Competence Assessment (MacCAT-CA) is false?

options.text: The assessment begins with a vignette of a hypothetical offence.
The MacCAT-CA comprises 30 items that are organized into five sections.

The MacCAT-CA differs notably from earlier competence assessment instruments (e.g. Competence to Stand Trial Assessment Instrument, Interdisciplinary Fitness Interview [IFI] and Fitness Interview Test [FIT]).
The MacCAT-CA is used to assess a defendant’s competence to stand trial.
The respondents are asked to make judgements about their own cases and explain their reasoning.

correct_answer.text: The MacCAT-CA comprises 30 items that are organized into five sections.

correct_answers.text: The MacCAT-CA comprises 30 items that are organized into five sections.

questions.explanation: The MacCAT-CA actually comprises 22 items organized into three sections: Understanding, Reasoning and Appreciation, not 30 items in five sections.

questions.question_text: A 26-year-old man was involved in a fight in the pub and has suffered head injuries. He was taken to the hospital and has been treated. Thereafter, his mother noted that he had non-fluent speech and seemed to be more depressed. He is likely to have suffered a head injury involving which part of the cortex?
questions.explanation: Injury to the left frontal lobe, particularly Broca’s area, produces non-fluent aphasia and can also affect mood regulation, leading to depression.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following neurochemicals would be capable of affecting one’s food intake?
questions.explanation: Cholecystokinin is a gut peptide that acts centrally to produce satiety and reduce food intake.

questions.question_text: Based on existing epidemiological studies, what has been estimated to be the prevalence of deliberate self-harm among young people in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Deliberate self-harm prevalence in UK adolescents is estimated at around 10% according to national surveys.

questions.question_text: Translation is the process in genetic expression whereby mRNA would serve as a template allowing the genetic code to be deciphered, and in turn allowing for the formation of a peptide chain. At which location does this take place?
questions.explanation: Translation occurs on ribosomes attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum, where mRNA is decoded and polypeptides are synthesized.

questions.question_text: Neuroimaging studies involving structural MRI have shown which of the following structural changes in patients with panic disorder?

options.text: Increase in medial temporal lobe volume
Reduction in medial temporal lobe volume

correct_answer.text: Reduction in medial temporal lobe volume

correct_answers.text: Reduction in medial temporal lobe volume

questions.explanation: Structural MRI studies in panic disorder have demonstrated a reduction in the volume of the medial temporal lobes, including the hippocampus.

questions.question_text: This is a concept that refers to the occurrence of an autosomal dominant disorder at earlier ages of onset or with greater severity in the succeeding generations. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Anticipation describes the phenomenon where successive generations exhibit earlier onset and/or increased severity of a genetic disorder.

questions.question_text: Previous epidemiological studies have identified that there is a high prevalence of self-harm among the Goth subculture in the United Kingdom. What is the estimated incidence of lifetime self-harm in that particular subculture?
questions.explanation: Lifetime self-harm prevalence among UK Goth youth has been reported at around 50% in survey studies.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cell types is responsible for the secretion of prolactin?
questions.explanation: Mammotropes (lactotropes) in the anterior pituitary produce and secrete prolactin.

questions.question_text: Rapid cycling bipolar disorder tends to affect roughly what percentage of patients?
questions.explanation: Rapid cycling is seen in approximately 13%–30% of patients with bipolar disorder, commonly cited around 20%.

questions.question_text: This is a concept that refers to the phenomenon in which an individual inherits both homologues of a chromosome pair from the same parent. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Uniparental disomy occurs when both copies of a chromosome are inherited from one parent instead of one from each.

questions.question_text: The old age psychiatrist has diagnosed Mr Smith with mild cognitive impairment. Mrs Smith, the caregiver, wants to know how this is different from dementia. Which one of the following statements is representative of the most important difference?

options.text: Patients with mild cognitive impairment tend to have a higher MMSE score as compared to those with dementia.
Patients with dementia tend to complain of more subjective memory loss.
Patients with dementia tend to have more objective evidence of cognitive impairment.
Patients with mild cognitive impairment tend to have preserved basic ADL and are able to still live independently.
Patients with dementia would have more significant decline from previously normal level of functioning.

correct_answer.text: Patients with mild cognitive impairment tend to have preserved basic ADL and are able to still live independently.

correct_answers.text: Patients with mild cognitive impairment tend to have preserved basic ADL and are able to still live independently.

questions.explanation: In mild cognitive impairment, patients maintain independence in basic activities of daily living, unlike in dementia.

questions.question_text: It has been known that vascular dementia accounts for what proportion of all the dementia in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Vascular dementia is the second most common cause of dementia in the UK, accounting for about 20% of cases.

questions.question_text: What has been estimated to be the life-time risk for adults in the general population of acquiring bipolar disorder?
questions.explanation: The lifetime prevalence of bipolar disorder in the general population is estimated at about 1%–1.5%.

questions.question_text: One of the following cell types has been described as the macrophages of the central nervous system. Which one of the following is the correct option?
questions.explanation: Microglia act as the resident immune cells (macrophages) of the central nervous system.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the function of the ribosome?

options.text: It helps to provide cellular energy.
It is the main site of DNA storage.
It helps in the post-translational modification process of the proteins.
It helps with the synthesis of new proteins.
It helps with the transcription process of DNA to mRNA.

correct_answer.text: It helps with the synthesis of new proteins.

correct_answers.text: It helps with the synthesis of new proteins.

questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the cellular organelles responsible for translating mRNA into polypeptide chains (new proteins).

questions.question_text: Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (CJD) has been known to be a very rare cause of a rapidly progressive dementia. Which one of the following causes the characteristic spongiform appearance that could be detected in this condition?

options.text: Vacuolar changes in the grey matter, especially in the cerebral and cerebellar cortex

correct_answer.text: Vacuolar changes in the grey matter, especially in the cerebral and cerebellar cortex

correct_answers.text: Vacuolar changes in the grey matter, especially in the cerebral and cerebellar cortex

questions.explanation: CJD is characterized by vacuolation (spongiform change) in the grey matter, particularly cortex and basal ganglia.

questions.question_text: When people with Down’s syndrome reach the age of 40 years, they have a high risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease. The gene that accounts for this association is
questions.explanation: The amyloid precursor protein gene is located on chromosome 21; trisomy 21 in Down’s syndrome leads to overexpression and increased Alzheimer’s pathology.

questions.question_text: Functions of astrocytes include the following, except

options.text: Providing metabolic support to the brain
Providing structural support to the brain

questions.explanation: Astrocytes support neurons and blood–brain barrier integrity and can remove debris, but myelin sheath formation is the role of oligodendrocytes.

questions.question_text: The ventral tegmental area is located in the
questions.explanation: The ventral tegmental area is part of the midbrain and is a key dopaminergic nucleus in the mesolimbic pathway.

questions.question_text: Which of the following enzymes are involved in the metabolism of serotonin?

options.text: GABA transaminase and glutamic acid decarboxylase

questions.explanation: Serotonin is metabolized by monoamine oxidase A (MAO-A) to 5-HIAA, which is further processed by aldehyde dehydrogenase.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a type of glutamate receptor?
questions.explanation: AMPA receptors are ionotropic glutamate receptors mediating fast excitatory neurotransmission.

questions.question_text: A 24-year-old man with schizophrenia complains of third-person auditory hallucinations. Which of the following gyri is involved?
questions.explanation: Heschl’s gyrus (primary auditory cortex) shows increased activation during auditory hallucinations in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old woman with borderline personality disorder wants to find out more about dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT). Which of the following statements regarding DBT is true?

options.text: DBT uses thinking and techniques drawn from Shinto philosophy emphasizing harmony with the environment.
DBT does not promote the use of metaphor as DBT is strongly influenced by cognitive behaviour therapy.
DBT does not promote the judicious use of humour or irreverence to reinforce the boundary between the therapist and the patient.
Dialectical thinking refers to the way of thinking that emphasizes the limitations of linear ideas about causation.
Out-of-therapy telephone contact by a case manager is usually available on a 24-hour basis to prevent self-harm.

correct_answer.text: Dialectical thinking refers to the way of thinking that emphasizes the limitations of linear ideas about causation.

correct_answers.text: Dialectical thinking refers to the way of thinking that emphasizes the limitations of linear ideas about causation.

questions.explanation: Dialectical thinking in DBT highlights the need to hold contrasting ideas and recognize that change can occur through synthesis of opposing perspectives.

questions.question_text: The following symptoms found in patients with bulimia nervosa are the focus of interpersonal therapy (IPT) except:

options.text: Binge eating, guilt and self-induced vomiting
Conflict avoidance and difficulty with role expectations
Confusion regarding the needs for closeness and distance
Social anxiety, sensitivity to conflict and rejection

correct_answer.text: Binge eating, guilt and self-induced vomiting

correct_answers.text: Binge eating, guilt and self-induced vomiting

questions.explanation: IPT targets interpersonal issues (role disputes, transitions, deficits, grief), not the specific behavioural symptoms of bulimia such as bingeing or purging.

questions.question_text: Which of the aforementioned medications would cause increased delta activity?
questions.explanation: The administration of antidepressant would cause an increase in delta activity.

questions.question_text: Which of the aforementioned medications would cause a decreased alpha activity, but an increased beta activity?
questions.explanation: In general, anxiolytics would cause an increased beta activity and a reduction in alpha activity.

questions.question_text: This particular class of medication would cause an increase in the low-frequency delta activity.
questions.explanation: Antipsychotics can cause an increase in beta activity and a reduction in alpha activity (at times).

questions.question_text: This particular class of medication would lead to only small EEG changes that are likely to be missed on recordings.
questions.explanation: It has been noted that therapeutic levels of lithium lead to only small effects that are likely to be missed on visual analysis of routine recordings.

questions.question_text: It is noted that 5-HT transmission from the caudal raphe nuclei and rostral raphe nuclei is increased in patients with this condition.
questions.explanation: It has been noted that the 5-HT transmission from the caudal raphe nuclei and rostral raphe nuclei is increased in patients with manic disorder.

questions.question_text: It is noted that in this condition, when there is an excess of 5-HT, there will be a reduction in the availability of DA. This might give rise to some of the symptoms such as reduced interest and withdrawal. Which condition is this?
questions.explanation: There is noted to be an interesting relationship between 5-HT and DA. When excess 5-HT is produced, there is a corresponding reduction in the availability of DA, which may give rise to negative symptoms in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: It is noted that in this condition, the 5-HT transmission from the rostral raphe nuclei to the temporal lobe is reduced.
questions.explanation: In Alzheimer’s dementia, 5-HT transmission from the rostral raphe nuclei to the temporal lobe is reduced.

questions.question_text: Presynaptic 5HT dysfunction is considered to be a state marked in this condition.
questions.explanation: Presynaptic 5-HT dysfunction is a state marker in depressive disorder, with reduced transmission from raphe nuclei.

questions.question_text: This neuropeptide has an inhibitory effect on the growth hormone release.
questions.explanation: Somatostatin has inhibitory effects on growth hormone release and is reduced in depression and Alzheimer’s.

questions.question_text: This is considered to be the smallest brain peptide, but it has the ability to reverse sedation caused by drugs.
questions.explanation: Thyrotropin-releasing factor is the smallest brain peptide and can reverse sedation by stimulating DA and ACh release.

questions.question_text: This neuropeptide is involved in appetite and feeding, as well as emotional behaviour.
questions.explanation: Cholecystokinin regulates appetite and feeding and is involved in emotional behaviour.

questions.question_text: This neuropeptide could be found in multiple locations, which include the cerebral cortex, hypothalamus, amygdala, hippocampus, autonomic ganglia and intestinal and respiratory tracts.
questions.explanation: Vasoactive intestinal peptide is found in cortex, hypothalamus, amygdala, hippocampus, autonomic ganglia and gut/respiratory tracts.

questions.question_text: Injections of this neuropeptide might lead to depressive symptoms such as reduced appetite and sex drive.
questions.explanation: Corticotrophin-releasing factor controls ACTH release and injections can produce depressive symptoms.

questions.question_text: These adverse drug reactions are consistent with the known pharmacological actions of the drug.
questions.explanation: Intolerance reactions are dose-related and consistent with the drug’s known pharmacological actions.

questions.question_text: These adverse drug reactions are not characteristic and predictable.
questions.explanation: Idiosyncratic reactions are unpredictable and not characteristic of the drug’s known effects.

questions.question_text: These adverse drug reactions involve the body’s immune system.
questions.explanation: Allergic reactions involve immune-mediated responses to the drug.

questions.question_text: Enzyme inhibition and enzyme induction are part of this process.
questions.explanation: Pharmacokinetic interactions include enzyme induction and inhibition affecting drug levels.

questions.question_text: This chromosome is involved in Edward’s syndrome.
questions.explanation: Edward’s syndrome (trisomy 18) involves chromosome 18.

questions.question_text: This chromosome is involved in Alzheimer’s disease.
questions.explanation: The presenilin 1 gene on chromosome 14 is implicated in Alzheimer’s disease.

questions.question_text: This chromosome is involved in Patau’s syndrome and Wilson’s disease.
questions.explanation: Patau’s syndrome and Wilson’s disease are linked to chromosome 13.

questions.question_text: Neuregulin is encoded on this chromosome.
questions.explanation: The neuregulin gene is located on chromosome 8.

questions.question_text: This chromosome is involved in autism.
questions.explanation: Autism has been linked to loci on chromosome 2.

questions.question_text: The focus of this form of dynamic therapy is to clarify the nature of the defences and its relationship to anxiety and impulses.
questions.explanation: Brief focal psychotherapy targets the nature of defences and their link to anxiety and impulses.

questions.question_text: The focus of this form of therapy is on the triangular conflict.
questions.explanation: Short-term dynamic psychotherapy centers on the triangular conflict.

questions.question_text: The focus of this form of dynamic therapy is to focus on the present.
questions.explanation: Time-limited psychotherapy emphasizes present-focused issues.

questions.question_text: This mutation involves a change to a single nucleotide. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: A substitution mutation changes a single nucleotide.

questions.question_text: Substitution of a purine for a purine. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: A transition is the substitution of one purine for another purine.

questions.question_text: Owing to the degeneracy of the genetic code, this mutation does not alter the amino acid being encoded. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: A silent mutation alters the DNA without changing the amino acid due to code degeneracy.

questions.question_text: This mutation results in the substitution of one amino acid for another. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: A missense mutation substitutes one amino acid for another.

questions.question_text: This mutation creates a new stop codon (UAA, UAG or UGA) and results in premature termination of translation. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: A nonsense mutation introduces a premature stop codon.

questions.question_text: The mutation usually results in a shortened (truncated) protein product. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: A frameshift mutation changes the reading frame and often truncates the protein.

questions.question_text: The morbid risk of the illness is determined within families, and rates of occurrence in the different degrees of relatives are compared with those in the general population. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Family studies assess familial clustering by comparing illness rates in relatives versus the general population.

questions.question_text: It compares the concordance rates of diagnosis in twins, both monozygotic and dizygotic, thus allowing researchers the possibility of dissecting the role of genes from that of the environment. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Twin studies compare monozygotic and dizygotic concordance to separate genetic from environmental influences.

questions.question_text: Genetic study to delineate inherited and environmental factors. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Adoption studies help distinguish genetic and environmental contributions by studying adoptees and their biological versus adoptive relatives.

questions.question_text: It compares the likelihood for the observed frequency of illness in a pedigree with multiple cases of affective disorder with those that can be predicted by different modes of transmission. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Segregation analysis uses statistical methods to test inheritance models against observed pedigrees.

questions.question_text: A 10-year-old girl presents with a small head, happy face, jerk movement and ataxia. She is known to have a history of epilepsy and learning disability.
questions.explanation: Angelman syndrome is caused by deletion on maternal chromosome 15, presenting with a 'happy' disposition.

questions.question_text: A 14-year-boy is referred to the early psychosis service. He has features of a round face, cleft palate, low-set ears, learning disability and congenital heart disease with frequent infections.
questions.explanation: DiGeorge syndrome (velocardiofacial syndrome) involves a microdeletion on chromosome 22.

questions.question_text: Acute encephalitis.

options.text: Diffuse slow activity with episodic, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical bursts of rhythmic waves
Unusual appearance of episodic discharges, recurring every 1–3 seconds and variable focal slow waves over the temporal areas
Periodic stereotyped repetitive discharges at a rate of 1 per second
High-amplitude, repetitive, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical, polyphasic sharp-wave and slow-wave complexes, occurring every 4–15 seconds

correct_answer.text: Diffuse slow activity with episodic, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical bursts of rhythmic waves

correct_answers.text: Diffuse slow activity with episodic, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical bursts of rhythmic waves

questions.explanation: Acute encephalitis EEG shows diffuse slow activity with episodic, bilaterally synchronous bursts of rhythmic waves.

questions.question_text: Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.

options.text: Diffuse slow activity with episodic, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical bursts of rhythmic waves
Unusual appearance of episodic discharges, recurring every 1–3 seconds and variable focal slow waves over the temporal areas
Periodic stereotyped repetitive discharges at a rate of 1 per second
High-amplitude, repetitive, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical, polyphasic sharp-wave and slow-wave complexes, occurring every 4–15 seconds

correct_answer.text: Periodic stereotyped repetitive discharges at a rate of 1 per second

correct_answers.text: Periodic stereotyped repetitive discharges at a rate of 1 per second

questions.explanation: CJD is characterized by periodic stereotyped repetitive discharges at about 1 per second.

questions.question_text: Herpes simplex encephalitis.

options.text: Diffuse slow activity with episodic, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical bursts of rhythmic waves
Unusual appearance of episodic discharges, recurring every 1–3 seconds and variable focal slow waves over the temporal areas
Periodic stereotyped repetitive discharges at a rate of 1 per second
High-amplitude, repetitive, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical, polyphasic sharp-wave and slow-wave complexes, occurring every 4–15 seconds

correct_answer.text: Unusual appearance of episodic discharges, recurring every 1–3 seconds and variable focal slow waves over the temporal areas

correct_answers.text: Unusual appearance of episodic discharges, recurring every 1–3 seconds and variable focal slow waves over the temporal areas

questions.explanation: Herpes simplex encephalitis shows episodic discharges every 1–3 seconds with focal slow waves over temporal areas.

questions.question_text: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis.

options.text: Diffuse slow activity with episodic, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical bursts of rhythmic waves
Unusual appearance of episodic discharges, recurring every 1–3 seconds and variable focal slow waves over the temporal areas
Periodic stereotyped repetitive discharges at a rate of 1 per second
High-amplitude, repetitive, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical, polyphasic sharp-wave and slow-wave complexes, occurring every 4–15 seconds

correct_answer.text: High-amplitude, repetitive, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical, polyphasic sharp-wave and slow-wave complexes, occurring every 4–15 seconds

correct_answers.text: High-amplitude, repetitive, bilaterally synchronous and symmetrical, polyphasic sharp-wave and slow-wave complexes, occurring every 4–15 seconds

questions.explanation: SSPE shows high-amplitude, repetitive, bilaterally synchronous polyphasic sharp-wave and slow-wave complexes every 4–15 seconds.
